title: 2022 Nissan Rogue Trims and Specs Comparison
summary: Compare 2022 Nissan Rogue trim levels, specs, and features. Learn the differences between S, SV, SL, and Platinum trims, plus the 1.5L VC-Turbo engine.
body_markdown:
The **[2022 Nissan Rogue](https://www.cargurus.com/research/2022-Nissan-Rogue-c32056)** is a top contender in the competitive compact crossover segment, combining sharp exterior styling, a family-friendly cabin, and smart interior storage. Following its full redesign for 2021, the 2022 Rogue gets a major mechanical upgrade: an all-new 1.5-liter Variable Compression Turbo 3-cylinder engine paired with an updated Xtronic CVT.


That powertrain lifts output to 201 horsepower and 225 lb-ft of torque while improving fuel economy to an EPA-estimated 37 mpg highway. Inside, the Rogue offers family-oriented touches like rear doors that open to nearly 90 degrees, optional Tri-Zone Automatic Temperature Control, and Nissan's Divide-N-Hide cargo management system.


The 2022 lineup spans four trim levels, running from budget-conscious everyday efficiency to near-luxury highway cruising with ProPilot Assist.

## 2022 Nissan Rogue Trim Levels Breakdown


### Nissan Rogue S


The S is the foundational entry-level trim, with a generous set of standard safety hardware and modern smartphone connectivity:


- 1.5-liter VC-Turbo 3-cylinder engine producing 201 horsepower and 225 lb-ft of torque
- Front-wheel drive with available Intelligent All-Wheel Drive
- 8-inch NissanConnect touchscreen with wired Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
- Nissan Safety Shield 360 with Automatic Emergency Braking and Pedestrian Detection, Blind Spot Warning, Rear Cross Traffic Alert, Lane Departure Warning, High Beam Assist, and Rear Automatic Braking
- 17-inch aluminum-alloy wheels and LED headlights with LED daytime running lights
- Cloth seating surfaces and 60/40 split-folding rear seats


The S covers strong standard turbo torque and full active safety coverage for value-driven shoppers.


### Nissan Rogue SV


The SV is the popular sweet spot of the lineup, unlocking the driver-assistance tech and daily comfort upgrades most buyers want:


- ProPilot Assist highway driving assistance
- 18-inch aluminum-alloy wheels and heated outside mirrors with LED turn signal indicators
- 8-way power-adjustable driver's seat with 2-way power lumbar support
- Dual-Zone Automatic Temperature Control and Nissan Intelligent Key with push-button ignition
- Remote Engine Start System with Intelligent Climate Control
- Wi-Fi hotspot capability and two rear USB charging ports
- Available SV Premium Package, which adds a dual-panel panoramic moonroof, leatherette seats, roof rails, and a hands-free power liftgate


### Nissan Rogue SL


The SL steps into near-luxury territory with better interior materials and practical utility upgrades:


- Leather-appointed seating with heated front seats and heated steering wheel
- Dual-panel panoramic moonroof and motion-activated power liftgate
- 19-inch aluminum-alloy wheels and roof rails
- Divide-N-Hide cargo management system
- Tri-Zone Automatic Temperature Control and memory settings for the driver's seat and outside mirrors
- Intelligent Around View 360-degree monitor
- Available SL Premium Package, which adds a 9-inch touchscreen, Bose premium audio, ProPilot Assist with Navi-link, and Traffic Sign Recognition


### Nissan Rogue Platinum


As the range-topping flagship, the Platinum arrives fully loaded with luxury materials, advanced displays, and upgraded audio:


- Quilted semi-aniline leather-appointed seats with heated rear outboard seats
- ProPilot Assist with Navi-link, which adjusts speed using navigation curve data and speed limit signs
- 12.3-inch fully digital instrument display and available 10.8-inch head-up display
- 9-inch NissanConnect touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay
- 10-speaker Bose premium audio system with dual-driver woofer
- Wireless charging pad and interior ambient lighting

## Powertrain & Specs: 1.5L VC-Turbo Performance & Fuel Economy


Unlike previous model years, every 2022 Rogue runs the same 1.5-liter VC-Turbo engine, which continuously varies its compression ratio to balance power against efficiency.


### The 1.5L VC-Turbo 3-Cylinder (201 hp)


The engine makes 201 horsepower and 225 lb-ft of torque through a re-engineered Xtronic CVT. Properly equipped, the Rogue tows up to 1,500 lbs.


### Fuel Economy by Drivetrain


- Front-wheel drive S and SV: an EPA-estimated 30 mpg city, 37 mpg highway, and 33 mpg combined
- Front-wheel drive SL and Platinum: up to 29 mpg city, 36 mpg highway, and 32 mpg combined
- Intelligent AWD models: 28 to 30 mpg city, 34 to 35 mpg highway, and 31 to 32 mpg combined depending on trim


## Which 2022 Nissan Rogue Trim is the Best Value?


For most buyers, the SV is the best overall value in the lineup. It adds the core technology buyers actually want, most notably ProPilot Assist, a power driver's seat, keyless access, and dual-zone climate control, while keeping running costs down. The optional SV Premium Package brings leatherette seating and a panoramic moonroof without stepping up to SL pricing.


If leather finishes and maximum cargo versatility matter more, the SL is a worthwhile upgrade, with standard leather, 19-inch wheels, and the Divide-N-Hide cargo system.


**Our pick:** Start with the SV for everyday technology and driver-assist value. Step up to the SL for leather comfort, or choose the Platinum if you want the digital displays, Bose audio, and quilted semi-aniline leather.
